title: Review of lab 1's chemotaxis-motility/swimevo (SID): S, I and D replicate on fresh seeds 3 and 4 (swimmers from a near-uniform noisy field by t~50, 8 and 5 persistent splits, generation 2 and 3), but division is reticulate (merge/split 1.23-1.30) and the population falls from ~31 to 10-12
summary: Labkit packs of threads/chemotaxis-motility/worlds/swimevo/world.py, unchanged, 160^2, t=0-1200. From a near-uniform field with small noise everywhere (sheet t=0), ~30 bodies condense by t~50 and swim (45 and 49 tracks move >= 1 body length, best 23.8 and 20.5). Division: 60 and 50 splits, 8 and 5 persistent, max generation 2 and 3, merges 74 and 65. Bodies at the end: 10 and 12 (max 31-32). The sheet shows the two alleles' colours shifting toward one allele over the run.

observations.S: pack/seed3/sheet.png t=0: near-uniform field with noise everywhere
observations.D: pack/seed3/lineage.png: 8 persistent splits, generation 2; seed 4: 5, generation 3

seeds_run.result: pass: S I D (8 persistent splits, gen 2)
pass: S I D (5 persistent splits, gen 3)

verdicts.limitation: Division is reticulate (merges exceed splits) and generations are short (2-3); the population declines (31 -> 10-12), as lab 1 noted. I did not examine the allele dynamics (H, L7) or run the neutral twin.
